-1 damage die step on opportunity attacks you make.
+1 spell save DC or attack for one spell.
Combat uses feet or 5-foot spaces. Movement can be split around actions and attacks. Difficult terrain costs 2 feet per foot. Severe terrain costs 3 feet per foot and may require a check.

Forced movement does not provoke opportunity attacks unless a feature explicitly says it does. Falling, flowing water, conveyor mechanisms, gravity changes, and living dungeon surfaces are common sources of forced movement.

Cargo matters. A creature carrying more Extraction Load than its safe capacity loses 10 feet of Speed, cannot Dash without a check, and has disadvantage on Acrobatics. Dropping a cargo harness is a free interaction if it was prepared for release.
Large weapons and broad formations are hindered; creatures may be unable to pass.
A hard impact or failed Dexterity save changes or collapses the terrain.
Spells of one school cost 1 less RP; an opposed school costs 1 more.
Failed saves or overcasting can add Corruption.
Verbal components and audible commands fail or require a check.
Swimming, buoyancy, current, and fire resistance rules apply.
Height, falling, climbing, and aerial control dominate.
The terrain reacts at the end of the round and can be wounded, fed, or pacified.
A faction, guardian, or dungeon-authority effect can issue commands through the area.

An attack roll is d20 + ability modifier + proficiency when proficient. A natural 1 misses. A natural 20 hits and doubles damage dice. Armor Class remains the primary defense, but cover, stance, shields, conditions, and reactions determine whether a target can survive concentrated attacks.
Replace one attack; Athletics or weapon check vs Athletics/Acrobatics. On success, held item falls in an adjacent space.
Bonus action Deception vs Insight. On success, gain advantage on the next melee attack this turn.
Reaction while Guarding; move 5 ft. and become the target of an attack against an adjacent ally.
Ready a ranged attack against movement through a named lane; the attack does not consume ammunition until triggered.
On a successful ranged hit, reduce target Speed by 10 ft. until it spends an action or succeeds on a Strength check.
After hitting in melee, move 5 ft. into the target’s vacated space if it retreats before your next turn.
Attack an object, shield, armor component, or construct joint. Damage applies to item durability rather than HP.
Replace one attack; Athletics vs Athletics/Acrobatics. On success, target falls Prone.
Action; move up to half Speed without provoking and gain +2 AC until movement ends.
Action; attach, lift, transfer, or protect up to one Extraction Load class of cargo.
A melee hit can force an immediate concentration check and prevents reactions with verbal components until target’s next turn.
Shove with disadvantage; on success push 10 ft. and remove Guard bonuses from adjacent allies.

Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Slashing, Thunder, and Corruption. Corruption damage cannot be resisted unless an effect explicitly protects against Corruption; it usually also creates a condition, mutation, or Unity Exposure.

Hit points represent endurance, luck, armor deflection, and minor injury. Wounds represent lasting trauma. A creature makes a Wound save when it drops to 0 HP, suffers damage equal to at least half its maximum HP from one source, or is struck by an effect marked Maiming. The save is Constitution, DC 10 or half the triggering damage, whichever is higher.
Gain one Wound. Each Wound imposes -1 on Constitution saves and maximum Hit Dice recovered per long rest.
Gain one Wound and roll on the Injury table.
Character is Critically Wounded: Speed -10 ft., cannot regain full HP, and dies on the next failed Wound save.
At 0 HP, a character is Unconscious and makes death saves at the start of each turn: 10+ success, 9- failure, three of either resolves the state.
A natural 20 restores 1 HP. A natural 1 causes two failures. Damage at 0 HP causes one failure, or two on a critical hit.
An action and DC 10 Medicine check stabilizes a dying creature. A healer’s kit succeeds automatically but consumes one use.
Resurrection restores life but does not automatically remove Wounds, Corruption, debt, legal death, or claims upon the recovered body.

An intelligent foe below one-quarter HP or with half its allies defeated makes a morale check unless Fanatical, Mindless, or controlled. Surrender can lead to ransom, recruitment, enslavement, interrogation, exchange, or release. These outcomes are economic and reputational decisions, not merely combat cleanup.

Each class retains its unique mechanic—Crescendo, Conviction, Blood Gauge, Momentum, Shapeshifting, Ki, Spell Matrix, Totems, Revelations, Oaths, and related systems. The shared combat rules do not replace those mechanics. They provide timing and limits so class resources can interact consistently.
One ally imposes Prone, Restrained, Marked, Judged, or Bleeding.
The next different ally to exploit it gains +2 damage or +1 save DC.
Two different schools affect the same target in one round.
The second caster may spend 1 RP to add a minor rider based on the school pair.
Two allies Shove, Press, or control the same enemy.
Move target 5 additional feet or remove one reaction.
One ally Guards while another harvests, repairs, or secures cargo.
The worker does not lose progress when damaged once.
Boss is Staggered and at a phase threshold.
One Hero ability may ignore resistance, never immunity.
